subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging
overview: Islam teaches Muslims to work hard and to help people who are truly in need. Begging, when a person is able to work, is discouraged because it harms dignity and the community. In this sub-strand you will name the people who deserve help, describe the evils of begging, and see how honest work helps to remove poverty.

lessons.title: Who deserves help, and why begging is an evil
objectives: Name the categories of people who deserve assistance.
Describe the evils of begging according to Islamic teachings.
lessons.intro: At the market you may see someone sitting with a hand stretched out, asking passers-by for money. Islam does not ignore people who are suffering, but it also warns against begging when a person can earn.
lessons.notes:
### People who deserve assistance
The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that asking people for money is not allowed except in three situations (Sahih Muslim):

- A debtor: a person who is carrying a heavy debt that he cannot pay. He may seek help until the debt is settled, then he should stop.
- A person struck by disaster: someone whose property has been destroyed by a flood, fire, drought or another calamity. He may seek help until he can stand on his own again.
- A destitute person: someone who is truly poor and does not have enough for basic needs. Responsible people in the community should be able to confirm that the need is real. He may seek help until he has enough, then he should stop.

These are the people Muslims should support with zakat, sadaqah and other help. Helping them is an act of kindness and worship.

### Why people beg
Some people beg because of real poverty, debt, sickness, old age, being an orphan, or losing property in a disaster. Others beg out of laziness, or because begging has become a habit, even though they could work. A Muslim should know the difference. The design of this lesson calls us to self-awareness: we avoid begging when we have no real justification.

### Evils of begging
- It lowers a person's dignity. The Prophet (S.A.W) said that the upper hand is better than the lower hand (Bukhari and Muslim). The upper hand is the one that gives; the lower hand is the one that asks.
- It can make a person stop trying. A habit of begging weakens hard work.
- It may involve lying, if someone pretends to be poorer than he is.
- It can take help away from people who are truly desperate.
- Begging without a real need is unlawful. The Prophet (S.A.W) taught that, apart from the three cases above, the person who begs is taking what is not allowed.

Islam wants every Muslim who is able to work to earn, and wants the community to carry those who truly cannot.

keyWords.meaning: a person who owes money that he or she must pay back
a person who is extremely poor and lacks basic needs
a sudden event such as a flood or fire that destroys property
asking people for money or food instead of earning it

examples.problem: A trader's shop burns down and he has no goods left. His neighbour is healthy but refuses to look for work and asks people for money every day. Who deserves assistance, and why?
steps: The trader lost his property through a disaster. He is in one of the three groups the Prophet (S.A.W) named.
The healthy neighbour can work. Begging without a real need is discouraged.
examples.answer: The trader deserves help until he can trade again. The neighbour should work instead of begging.

activity.title: Who should we support?
steps: In groups, list the three categories of people who deserve support: debtors, those who lose property through disaster, and the destitute.
For each category, give one example a learner might see in the community.
Discuss the evils of begging according to the teachings of Islam.
Write the points in your notebook and present them to the class, taking turns to speak.

practice.question: Name the three categories of people who may seek help according to the teaching of the Prophet (S.A.W).
practice.answer: A person with a heavy debt, a person whose property is destroyed by a disaster, and a person who is truly destitute.

practice.question: What is meant by 'the upper hand is better than the lower hand'?
practice.answer: The hand that gives is better than the hand that asks.

practice.question: Give two evils of begging.
practice.answer: Any two: it lowers dignity; it discourages hard work; it may involve lying; it can take help from the truly needy; begging without need is unlawful.

practice.question: Why might a person beg after a flood destroys the family farm?
practice.answer: The family has lost its property through a disaster and may need help until they can stand again.

summary: Debtors, victims of disaster and the destitute deserve help.
Begging is not allowed for a person who can earn.
The giving hand is better than the asking hand.

lessons.title: Honest work as a way out of poverty
objectives: Describe ways of earning an honest income.
Explain how work helps to eradicate poverty.
Show appreciation for hard work in daily life.
lessons.intro: The Prophet (S.A.W) honoured people who earned their food with their own hands. A small honest job is better than stretching out a hand when you are able to work.
lessons.notes:
### Work is honourable
The Prophet (S.A.W) said that nobody has ever eaten better food than what he earned by the work of his own hands, and that Prophet Dawud (A.S.) used to eat from the work of his hands (Bukhari). He also taught that it is better for a person to take a rope, collect firewood, carry it and sell it than to beg from people who may give or refuse (Bukhari).

These teachings foster hard work. A Muslim does not look down on a lawful job, even if it looks simple.

### Ways of earning income
People generate income in many lawful ways:

- Farming: growing crops such as maize, beans, vegetables or fruit and selling the surplus.
- Keeping livestock: cows, goats, sheep or poultry for milk, meat or eggs.
- Trade: buying goods and selling them in a shop or at the market.
- Crafts: tailoring, carpentry, pottery, weaving or repairing items.
- Employment: working for a person, a farm, a school or a company and receiving wages.
- Services: teaching, cutting hair, washing clothes, or transporting goods.

A child in Grade 4 is not expected to run a business. You prepare for work by studying, helping with chores, learning a skill from a parent or relative, and refusing to ask for money you do not need.

### How work eradicates poverty
- Work puts food on the table without depending on begging.
- A working person can save a little and meet needs such as school, medicine and shelter.
- Workers can give sadaqah and become the upper hand.
- Honest work builds the family and the nation, because goods and services are produced.
- It protects dignity and teaches responsibility and integrity.

Poverty is not removed by wishing. It is reduced when people who can work do so, and when the community supports those who truly cannot. A Muslim thanks Allah for strength and uses that strength to earn.

keyWords.meaning: money earned from work, trade or another lawful source
the state of not having enough for basic needs
voluntary charity given to please Allah

examples.problem: Yusuf wants new shoes. He can ask strangers for coins, or he can help his uncle in the vegetable stall on Saturday and save what he is given. Which choice agrees with Islamic teaching?
steps: He is not a debtor, a disaster victim or destitute. He wants something extra.
Helping at the stall is honest work and keeps his dignity.
examples.answer: He should help his uncle and save, instead of begging.

activity.title: Ways of earning
materials: Pictures of farms, markets and crafts if available
steps: In pairs, list as many lawful ways of earning or generating income as you can.
Choose three and say what skill or tool each one needs.
Discuss how each kind of work can help a family leave poverty.
Present your list in class and write it in your notebook.

practice.question: What did the Prophet (S.A.W) say is better than begging: selling firewood, or sitting and asking people?
practice.answer: Collecting firewood and selling it is better than begging.

practice.question: Name three lawful ways of earning income.
practice.answer: Any three: farming, keeping livestock, trade, crafts such as tailoring or carpentry, employment for wages, or offering a service.

practice.question: Give two ways in which work helps to eradicate poverty.
practice.answer: Any two: it provides food and needs without begging; a person can save; workers can help others; it produces goods and services; it protects dignity.

practice.question: What can a Grade 4 learner do now to value work?
practice.answer: Study hard, help with chores, learn a skill, and avoid asking for money without a real need.

summary: The best food is what a person earns with his or her own hands.
Farming, trade, crafts, employment and services are lawful ways to earn.
Honest work reduces poverty and lets a Muslim help others.

quiz.question: Which person deserves assistance according to the teaching studied?
options: A healthy person who dislikes work
A family whose house and goods were destroyed by a flood
A trader who wants a second shop for pride
quiz.explanation: Loss of property through disaster is one of the three situations in which help may be sought.

quiz.question: A debtor may seek help until…
options: he becomes the richest person in town
quiz.explanation: Help for a debtor is until the heavy debt is paid, then he should stop asking.

quiz.question: Who is a destitute person?
quiz.answer: A person who is extremely poor and lacks basic needs.
quiz.explanation: The destitute are among those who deserve support.

quiz.question: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Which hand is the upper hand?
quiz.explanation: The Prophet (S.A.W) praised the hand that gives over the hand that receives.

quiz.question: Which of these is an evil of begging?
options: It can become a habit that stops a person from working
It is the same as zakat
quiz.explanation: Begging without need weakens hard work and lowers dignity.

quiz.question: Why is pretending to be poor in order to get money wrong?
quiz.answer: It is a lie, and it can take help away from people who are truly in need.
quiz.explanation: Islam forbids lying and wants charity to reach those who deserve it.

quiz.question: According to the Hadith, which food is the best?
options: Food earned by one's own hands
quiz.explanation: The Prophet (S.A.W) said nobody has eaten better food than what he earned by his own work.

quiz.question: Which of these is a lawful way of generating income?
quiz.explanation: Crafts such as tailoring are honest work.

quiz.question: How does honest work help to eradicate poverty?
quiz.answer: It provides for needs, allows saving, and lets a person help others instead of depending on begging.
quiz.explanation: Work is the means Islam encourages for removing poverty.

quiz.question: What should a person do after receiving enough help to stand again?
options: Stop asking and work if able
quiz.explanation: The permission to ask ends when the need has been met.

sources: KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 5.0 Akhlaq (Moral Teachings), Sub-strand 5.2.1 Prohibitions in Islam: Evils of Begging
Sahih Muslim: begging is not permissible except for three cases (debt, calamity, and confirmed poverty)
Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim: the upper hand is better than the lower hand; Sahih al-Bukhari: earning by one's own hands, and selling firewood rather than begging
